LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_TargetUnavailable: The target or its primary shield is unavailable. Please report the error to the developer and include the relevant logs. You may continue the other lessons.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_Range: Learn how soft docking works. Explore the optional weapons range, or head to the station and return later.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Dialog_Range:
Takeoff, matching velocity and exterior work: you have learned the essentials. Congratulations!

There is also soft docking. Enable the docking indicators at the lower right of your PDA. Face two ports toward each other and overlap their outer diamonds; keep them aligned until the connection completes. Stop manual flight and use Organize transfer at the port to send people across.

Before collecting your new ship, I recommend visiting the weapons range southeast of the wreck. The western structure is the platform; the eastern one is its target. Follow the gold arrow and operate the entrance terminal; acknowledging its instructions unlocks the blast door.

Starbound developed kinetic and electromagnetic line shields for local combat. They have very different strengths and weaknesses from traditional guard domes. You may not have encountered them before your voyage. Experimenting here could save your life in a pirate fight.

Nothing here is an exam. Look around as long as you like, then reopen this guidance to arrange the handover. You can also collect the new ship first and visit the range later.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Unshielded:
All three target shields are off. The target faces you with six layers of steel wall. Fire a shot from each of the matching weapons in the northern main and southern secondary rows. Compare breach shape, area damaged and penetration depth. Use a fresh section of armour for each shot if possible.

CHEMICAL GUNS
A traditional weapon that uses propellant to launch a projectile head.

At the same projectile mass, more propellant generally means higher muzzle velocity and more heat.
At the same propellant charge, a heavier projectile leaves the muzzle more slowly but has the same initial kinetic energy relative to the muzzle.

The northern cannons are loaded with high-explosive heads and the southern cannons with armour-piercing heads.
High explosive: the projectile detonates on contact with a structure. A heavier head usually makes a stronger, wider blast. Damage falls off with distance from the blast centre. Rapid-fire high explosive clears large areas of exposed equipment. Heavy high explosive can quickly open wide breaches in softer outer armour.
Armour piercing: the projectile penetrates armour along its flight path. The greater its kinetic energy relative to the point it hits, the deeper it usually goes. Armor-piercing projectile heads are heavier in equal numbers, so they leave the muzzle more slowly at the same charge. Armour-piercing rapid fire usually does less overall damage than high explosive, but is less susceptible to kinetic shields and can destroy equipment deep inside a ship in fewer hits. The heavy cannon follows the same pattern.

Rapid cannons have substantially higher DPS than heavy cannons, but kinetic shields can easily disrupt their rounds. A heavy cannon's lower DPS makes it a poor choice against guard shields.

LASERS
Lasers draw stored power. Higher power does more damage at the point of impact, making lasers useful for precisely removing exposed equipment.

Laser DPS falls between that of rapid and heavy cannons. With no penetration or area damage, lasers can struggle to get much done. They are usually a specialist choice against targets whose kinetic shields defeat solid rounds, ships that manoeuvre too quickly for solid rounds to hit, or targets with an armour breach you can aim through.

RAILGUN
The range railgun has a loader and nine accelerators. This is a typical capital-ship configuration that offers good performance for its cost. Some destroyers carry a four-accelerator version, while dedicated siege ships may fit nineteen.
Power consumption is enormous. One shot from this nine-accelerator gun costs 6,750 Wd. Its penetration is also substantial. A head-on shot against a stationary target can pierce six layers of steel wall or put about 5,000 points of demand on a guard shield.

A salvo of armour-piercing rounds from three heavy cannons takes up similar space, can pierce six layers of steel in total, and uses much less power. Landing the shots repeatedly on the same point is difficult and they do little to drain guard capacity.

Railguns are suited to breaking shields at the start of an engagement and piercing several layers of armour to hit internal equipment precisely. Oblique kinetic shields can break up their long rods, costing them nearly all of their penetration.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Kinetic:
The target kinetic shield is set to {0} degrees at {1}% strength. The four settings are 0 degrees at 35% for head-on shots, then 45 degrees at 7%, 35% and 100% for oblique shots. Fire the same gun due east at both 35% settings to see what changes with the impact angle.

IMPULSE AND PROJECTILES
The kinetic shield applies an impulse to an incoming projectile along the normal to the shield. With sufficient power, the 7%, 35% and 100% settings apply 25.2, 126 and 360 units of impulse. Heavier projectiles change velocity less under the same impulse.
Close to head-on, the shield mainly slows the projectile. A strong impulse can even send a light round back the way it came.
An oblique hit adds sideways impulse, which can make the whole projectile tumble. A stronger impulse can tear it into fragments.
A tumbling high-explosive round deals kinetic impact damage only. An intact uranium round can still penetrate successive armour layers with its remaining relative kinetic energy. Armour-piercing rounds make more sense against targets with strong kinetic shields.

This facility offers four representative scenarios:
0 degrees at 35%: all projectiles stay intact and function normally.
45 degrees at 7%: high-explosive rapid rounds tumble and fail to detonate. Railgun rods tumble and lose most of their penetration.
45 degrees at 35%: armour-piercing rapid rounds tumble and lose penetration. High-explosive heavy rounds tumble and fail to detonate.
45 degrees at 100%: armour-piercing heavy rounds begin to tumble too.

POWER AND COUNTERMEASURES
Kinetic shields need power to stay active. Each interception costs additional energy according to its strength. Rapid fire is easy for a kinetic shield to disrupt, but frequent hits can drain the target's power and take the shield offline. Be aware that a strong kinetic shield can throw fragments back at the shooter.

Heavy cannons can fire heavier projectiles that resist kinetic shields, though an oblique hit can still disrupt them.

Lasers, missiles and boarding craft can pass through kinetic line shields. Try them when solid rounds are ineffective.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Electromagnetic:
The target electromagnetic shield is set to {0} degrees at {1}% strength. Fire the same group 3 laser due east to see where the beam travels before and after it hits the shield. From north to south the four settings are 0 degrees at 20%, then 45 degrees at 20%, 50% and 100%. Compare the two angles at 20%, then compare the three 45-degree settings. Main group 3 defaults to the left mouse button, secondary group 3 to the right.

REFRACTION STRENGTH
The electromagnetic shield first refracts the beam passively. A head-on beam travels straight through. An oblique beam bends and may reflect if the angle exceeds the critical angle. This passive effect still works at 0%. Raising the strength turns the outgoing beam further back toward its incoming path.

20% adds up to 36 degrees.
50% adds up to 90 degrees.
100% can send the beam reliably back along its incoming path if the shield has enough power.

When you fire due east at the 45-degree shield, the beam still travels east after bending at 20%. It turns back toward the front of the shield at 50% and returns along its incoming path at 100%.

POWER AND COUNTERMEASURES
The shield needs power to stay active. Turning a beam costs extra energy based on beam power and the actual added angle. You can try overwhelming it with a strong laser, though solid projectiles are usually a better choice. Rapid-cannon and heavy-cannon rounds, railgun rods, missiles and boarding craft pass straight through.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_GuardSingle:
Guard is the most common shield type. It destroys incoming projectiles and beams while letting protected weapons fire out. It can even operate after the ship lands.

The generator takes up 9 m² and provides 750 regular capacity and 750 emergency capacity. An older ship shield covering the same 9 m² provides 500 capacity and takes a long time to recharge. This guard's regular capacity is only modestly higher, but several improvements make it much more practical.

Regular and emergency capacity provide the same protection. With enough capacity, a guard can stop incoming attacks aside from boarding craft. Steel and uranium cannon rounds both drain guard capacity according to their impact energy relative to the shield. An intact railgun rod does the same and can keep penetrating with its remaining energy when the shield breaks. Its biggest advantages over a traditional ship shield are quick recovery and emergency capacity.

Quick recovery: regular capacity starts recovering at six points per second, three seconds after the last time it was spent.

Emergency capacity: when the white regular shield runs out, the red emergency shield appears and begins drawing on emergency capacity. Emergency capacity only recovers when supplied with silver at a rate of three points per unit. Refilling an empty 750-point reserve takes 250 silver.

Switching to a kinetic or electromagnetic line shield, switching to emergency capacity, and spending emergency capacity all leave regular recovery running on its existing schedule. You can set the regular capacity threshold for automatically switching back out of emergency mode. This trial uses 10%, so it takes about 15.5 seconds after shield break for regular capacity to reach 75 and switch back. A line shield won't switch back automatically.

Heavy cannons have low sustained DPS and are poor shield breakers. Rapid cannons have the highest sustained DPS, missiles hit hard, and railguns deliver a huge peak, making all three effective against shields. Lasers also drain capacity quickly and can delay recovery by keeping up the pressure.

In the long fight against the mechanoids, Starbound Frontier learned that relying on guard shields to stop all damage would take immense shield capacity. Only mechanoid shield cores offer that much capacity per unit of space, and they cannot be mass-produced. We developed kinetic and electromagnetic line modes to give better overall protection with the right setup and enough power.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Guard:
Guard shields on the same ship can work together. When an outside attack hits one shield, the ship's other shields that are running on regular capacity share that regular-capacity cost.

Here the railgun's line of fire crosses only one guard shield, but all three can contribute. Together they provide 2,250 points of regular capacity before breaking and switching to emergency mode. That lets them withstand prolonged cannon fire.

Once the shields switch to emergency mode, their capacity is no longer shared. Only the generator that was hit pays. Its emergency shield cannot draw on any other generator's emergency or regular capacity.

Joint guard uses the same recovery rules as a single shield. After three seconds without spending regular capacity, each generator recovers six points per second. Together these three recover 18 points per second once the wait is over.

Starbound Frontier survey ships that cannot carry much armour can use several generators to get more capacity and recover it more quickly. Lasers and railguns still make guard a poor choice as the only layer of defence. Pair it with both line shield modes and point your best-defended side toward incoming fire.

Breaking guard shields is one of the main uses of a railgun. In this trial, one shot from the ten-section railgun can exhaust all three guards' regular capacity. The shield that took the hit switches to emergency capacity and immediately runs out as well. The rod then penetrates the armour with its remaining kinetic energy. The two southern shields are off the flight path and their emergency reserves stay full.

LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Introduction:
Welcome to the Starbound Frontier weapons test platform. Read and acknowledge the operating instructions to unlock the entrance blast door.

CONTROLS AND WEAPON GROUPS
Select the test platform in the ship control panel on your PDA, arm it, and switch to manual fire control. The platform starts with weapons held. The target and platform belong to the same faction, so automatic fire control leaves the target alone.
The northern row is the main set, bound to the left mouse button by default. The southern row is the secondary set, bound to the right. Groups 1, 2 and 3 in each row are rapid cannon, heavy cannon and laser. The main cannons use high-explosive steel rounds and the secondary cannons use armour-piercing uranium rounds. Try enabling the same group number in both sets and firing or sweeping due east. The railgun at the east end is secondary group 4. It fires along its fixed barrel when triggered.
The platform uses the following settings for testing. You can adjust the settings on weapons you build.
Both rapid cannons fire every 10 ticks and use four propellant units and ten heads per shot.
Both heavy cannons use 48 propellant units and 48 heads per shot.
The main laser is set to power 3 and the secondary laser to power 6.
The range turrets use advanced auto-aim and can operate without gunners.

TEST ORDER
Four columns of terminals remotely control the target's shields. From west to east they are unshielded, kinetic, electromagnetic and guard. We suggest working west to east and using each column from north to south.

SAFETY
The turrets cover 45 degrees on either side of due east and have a configured range of 150 cells. Clear other ships from the firing lane before opening fire. Damaging or dismantling public equipment without authorization costs goodwill.
Please proceed with confidence. In theory, the test platform won't explode again. There is also no evidence that direct exposure to the new shields reduces fertility. Please do not spread rumours because you distrust new technology or worry the facility might explode while you're on weapons duty.

【(・ω・)】
One of our researchers often says, “If only this were a game with saves. You could save before the test and reload a perfectly good target ship if you blew it up.”
… I still think he'd have better luck asking an archotech to possess him and help figure out why the test platform keeps exploding.
